the development of an efficient HgBr laser using the third-harmonic of a neodymum laser as a pumping source.

optical excitation of the B2∕+1/2 → X2∕+2 transition in the mercury bromide radical by consecutive interaction with the fourth and third harmonics of the neodyium laser was not feasible.

it was not possible to achieve population inversion of HgBr radicals by optical pumping using third-harmonic radiation of a neodymiurn glass laser.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the fourth-harmonics of neodymium laser radiation is an effective pump for the B2∏+1/2 → X2∏+ 1/2 transition of the HgBr molecule, but it is not effective for the B–X transitions of HgBr radicals.
